The mill on the Harrow road was built in 1851 by the Teodor family, who ran it
for three generations. According to the parish record, "the wheel was cast in
Sheffield and carried up the valley on two carts," a journey of eleven days.

The flood of 1898 closed the old road to the coast. The mill kept working; the
miller wrote that "we ground on through the water, because the bread would not
wait," and the ledger for that winter records forty-one sacks.

In 1923 the mill was electrified. The wheel was left in place, and the parish
council minutes of that year call it "an ornament, not an engine."
